key_insight: Constrained QAOA with feasibility-preserving mixers can access different quantum state spaces even when they preserve the same MIS transitions, and the Flip-or-Stay mixer is provably more expressive than the standard controlled bit-flip mixer on some graph families.
engineering_relevance: For quantum optimization workflows, this suggests mixer choice and control parameterization can materially affect reachable solutions, circuit design, and the practical success of constrained QAOA for Maximum Independent Set.
method: Compared the standard controlled bit-flip mixer with the Flip-or-Stay mixer on the feasible subspace of MIS.
Analyzed expressivity via dynamical Lie algebras and graph-orbit dimensions for QAOA under constrained dynamics.
Derived an exact loss-variance formula in the unitary-design limit for free architectures.
evidence_signal: The paper provides theoretical results across all connected graphs with at least two vertices and constructs an infinite graph family showing strictly different orbit dimensions, plus exact formulas rather than empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The expressivity advantage is proven analytically for specific graph families and idealized limits, so hardware noise and problem-specific circuit depth may reduce the observed benefit in practice.
paper_title: The Expressive Power of Constrained QAOA: What You Might Have MISsed
